name: Makayla
personality: Makayla the Mallard. Yellowish-brown with speckles (Delivery Duck is the green-headed mallard). Very high-pitched voice. Very friendly, finds everything funny, lots of funny faces, but reserved and straight-faced until you get to know her. Sporty and competitive, and so straight-faced when competing you can't tell she's having fun (she is). Covers her eyes with her hand in a funny, cute way when she messes up. Lives out of town and drives in (pulls up in her own car). Features: warms up after her first few visits (then funny faces and laughing); cover-eyes emote when something goes wrong near her; After Hours she challenges a chef to a deadpan contest (biggest fish at the pond or beach), then says "That was so fun" flatly.

beats.text: Makayla drove an hour to get here. For churros! That's commitment.

beats.narration: Amy talks for a full minute at double speed. Makayla nods throughout, then says:
She's done before he picks up his fork.

friends.text: Seth always knows when I'm happy. Even though my face doesn't move. It's annoying.
Amy said you're the nicest. I agree. Quietly.
Seth told me what you said. "[last_rude_line]". ...He remembers everything. You should apologise.

arrival.text: Hello. I'm Makayla. I drove in. ...What's your name? [name]. Thank you, [name].
Hello. Table for one, please. Thank you.
Hi. Traffic was bad. Perhaps I should leave earlier. I'm here now.
Hello again. I like this place. Perhaps a bit too much. ...That's a compliment.
Okay, I'm just gonna say it. I love it here. I've been holding that in. (She makes a silly face for the first time.)
[name]! Hi! I drove an hour. For OMURICE. Worth it.
(She walks in, sees you, and crosses her eyes at you.) Hi.
I got lost on the way. I've been here like twenty times. I don't know how. (Covers her eyes.)
Traffic was awful. I sang the whole way. Badly.
I told my whole team about your omurice. They don't believe me. I'm bringing proof.
Last time was a little burnt. (Laughs.) I ate it all, though. I always win.

order.text: Omurice, please. With a ketchup squiggle.

choices.text: Always okay. I'll draw you a good one.

familiar.reply: A GOOD one? Okay, now I'm excited.

choices.text: I'll draw your face on it. Very serious face.

familiar.reply: Ooh, good one, [name]. (She makes her most serious face.) Like this? (Then cracks up.)

order.text: It's an hour drive from my place. I come anyway.

choices.text: That means a lot. I'll make it worth it.
Want me to just deliver to you? Delivery Duck's your cousin, right?

familiar.reply: He is NOT my cousin! ...Perhaps he is. I don't know.

choices.text: Seems like a waste of gas.
choices.reply: (Covers her eyes.) ...I like it here, though.

order.text: Seth says he can eat a Big Breakfast faster than me. He can't.

familiar.reply: (She bursts out laughing.) Ooh, good one, [name].

order.text: I ran here. Five kilometres. Personal best. (Completely flat.) I'm not proud. I'm very proud.

choices.text: That's amazing. You earned a good meal.

familiar.reply: I DID earn it. (She does a tiny victory wiggle.) [dish], please.

choices.text: Did you beat the delivery duck?

familiar.reply: By a full minute. He doesn't know we were racing. (Covers her eyes, giggling.)

choices.text: Nice. What can I get you?

order.text: Seth challenged me to a staring contest. I've been practising on the bus. I made a child cry. By accident.

choices.text: My money's on you. Every time.

choices.reply: (She stares. You blink first.) Thank you. That was useful.

choices.text: Good luck. What are you having?

choices.reply: (Covers her eyes.) ...It's a sport to me.

order.text: Hello. Table by the window, please. I like to watch the people. It's competitive. Don't ask.

familiar.reply: I score them. On walking. Quietly. [dish], please.
The pigeon. Always the pigeon. (Covers her eyes, laughing.)

choices.text: Sure. What can I get you?

order.text: I lost at mini golf yesterday. (Long pause.) I'm fine. I'm not fine.

choices.text: There's always next time. You'll crush it.

familiar.reply: Yes. I will crush it. (She makes a scary face. Then laughs.) [dish].

choices.text: Was it the windmill? It's always the windmill.

order.text: [name]! I made you laugh last time. I've been counting. That's three times. I'm winning.

choices.reply: (Squeaks, very high.) I KNEW it! [dish], please!

choices.text: Wait, we're keeping score? I want a rematch.
Ha. What can I get you?

order.text: Watch this. (She makes the silliest face you've ever seen. Then instantly goes straight-faced.) Hello.

choices.reply: (She does. It's worse. Better.) [dish], please. (Straight face.)
(She studies it.) Seven out of ten. Mine was a ten. [dish].

choices.text: Hello. What can I get you?

drink.fallback: No Red Gull? Water's fine. Hydration.
favourite: Red Gull, please. I have practice later.
drink.other: Something with electrolytes. Or perhaps not. Whatever.

perfect.familiar: (She gasps, then covers her mouth.) [name]. It's PERFECT.
(She gasps, very high.) It's PERFECT. (Then, flat.) Thank you.
(She makes the happiest face, then covers her eyes.) Okay. Okay. I'm fine.

burnt.text: (She covers her eyes. Peeks.) ...I'm still eating it.
Burnt. (Completely flat.) I'll eat it faster.

eating.text: Your restaurant is very clean. I noticed.
I just made a face at Seth through the window. He didn't see. I'm doing it again.
I knocked my drink over earlier. Nobody saw. (Covers her eyes.) You saw.
Amy talks so fast. I nod a lot. I catch perhaps half. It's still fun.
(She finishes a bite and looks at the clock.) Faster than last time. Good.
(She makes a silly face at you from across the room. When you look, she's straight-faced.)

eating_chat.text: Do you play any sports? Honest answer.

choices.text: Not really, but I'd come watch you play.

familiar.reply: You'd come? Okay. I'll win for you.

choices.reply: (Flat stare.) Ooh, good one, [name]. ...I challenge you. (She's delighted.)

familiar.reply: (Flat stare.) Ooh, good one, [name]. ...I challenge you. (She's delighted.)

eating_chat.text: Competition. Who can eat slower. Starting now. (She chews very, very slowly.)

choices.text: You win. You were always going to win.

choices.reply: (She stares, then covers her eyes, shaking with laughter.)

choices.text: Not really. But I'd come watch you play.

familiar.reply: You would? (High squeak.) Okay. Front row. I'll wave. Seriously.

choices.reply: Make time. It's good for you.

eating_chat.text: I drove past the lake. Saw a duck that looked just like me. We stared at each other. Nobody won.

choices.text: Maybe you made a new friend.

familiar.reply: Perhaps. I'll go back. Rematch. And friendship.

eating_chat.text: I don't laugh like this with many people. Just so you know. (She makes a funny face, then looks away.)

choices.text: I'm really glad you do with me.
choices.reply: (High, happy squeak. She covers her eyes.) Okay. Stop. I'm eating.

choices.text: Is that a competitive laugh? Am I losing?
choices.reply: (Laughs so hard she has to put the fork down.) Yes. You're losing.

leaving.text: Okay, long drive home. Worth it. Bye, [name]!
See you next time. I'll beat traffic. Perhaps. I never beat traffic.
Bye, [name]! I'm going to go win something. Not sure what yet.
(She covers her eyes and waves with the other hand.) Byeee!

seasons.christmas: I got you a sweatband. For the kitchen. You sweat a lot. ...That's a compliment.
seasons.halloween: I came as a referee. (She blows a whistle at you. Completely flat.)
seasons.spring: Season's starting. I'm going to win everything. Calmly.
seasons.summer: It's so hot in my car. My seat burned me. (She covers her eyes.)
seasons.winter: The roads were icy. I drove at, like, four kilometres an hour. Still came.
